title: Cevahir Zihin and Cevahir AI: a Living Evidence Mind and Research Reports
description:
Release v7 (2026.11.24): Cevahir Zihin, a living evidence mind, described in full in English. The paper Cevahir Zihin: a Living Evidence Mind (CEV-2026-11, docs/research/living_evidence_mind_2026_11_24/PAPER.md) describes a learning system with no neural network, weight matrix, embedding or gradient: whatever it perceives becomes a unit, every relation a tie that keeps graded evidence for and against it separately by origin (sensed, told, imitated, its own act, inferred, imagined), read by one rule (e = c(f - 1/2) + 1/2, c = W/(W+1), the NARS expectation) and learned at every moment, with the evidence of any single experience exactly retractable through a ledger. On this core 75 mechanisms were built one at a time, each measured with its negative results; several were measured and not kept.

Results reported: having watched about 1,090 of the published SCAN training commands twice, the mind answers every command of the six published SCAN test files exactly (26,227 of 26,227), where Transformers trained from scratch on the same dialogues of the generated splits answer almost none (0 of 844 within the window, 1 of 7,706 at every length); COGS stays at 0, with its causes measured. On 13,290 Turkish sentences of private documents (only counts published), cued with the first two words of 200 read sentences, the mind after one reading (about 320 s of one processor core) says a read sentence in 146 to 151, a 7.3M-parameter Transformer trained from random weights for an hour on the same machine in 47. A grounded meaning layer joins perception and words in the same calculus: asked who does what in situations never described it answers 48 (Turkish) and 54 (English) of 72, a Transformer given the scene as tokens 29 and 42; naming an object of an unseen colour stays below that Transformer (16 and 19 of 23 against 21 and 23). Speed work kept every answer bit-identical (median answer 2.70 s to 0.64 s).

This release also holds an open mind (minds/cevahir-open.zihin.gz): the program's whole mind raised from nothing on public material only (lessons of public knowledge, school subjects, first dialogue files; 19,040 moments, 132,229 ties; every word it holds is a word of those files), with its recipe, sources, digest and study record. The Turkish documents of earlier releases (the first ten research records, the Turkish technical book, the Turkish theory and guide) were withdrawn from the repository by their author on 2026-11-20; each is replaced by a note, and their full texts remain in release v6 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24279940). The ten reports keep English editions with their abstracts and findings.

Versioned open-source research archive by Muhammed Yasin Yılmaz: eleven individually identified research reports/preprints (CEV-2026-01 to CEV-2026-11), the Cevahir Zihin implementation (zihin/), the Cevahir AI engine, reproducible experiments with their result rows, and preserved negative results. The worlds are small and generated, the Transformer comparisons are in a small-data regime on one processor, and the reports have not undergone external peer review. No claim of consciousness, general intelligence or novelty beyond what is measured is made. AI assistance was used for code, computational experiments, literature review and drafting. The DOI identifies this archived version; it does not certify scientific correctness. Start at docs/publications/README.md and docs/ZIHIN_THEORY.md.
